articleTitle: De-Dimensionalization and Scaling for the Dynamic Analysis and Optimization of Compliant Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: With this work we contribute to the dynamic analysis and optimization of compliant mechanisms with respect to their natural frequencies. For this, we extend the analytical background of the already existing calculation tool CaTEf, enabling the scaling of given compliant mechanisms to a desired first natural frequency. To do this, we first carry out the de-dimensionalization of the frequency calculation in order to decouple it from the dimension and material properties of the mechanisms. The choice of the appropriate de-dimensioning parameters leads to a relationship that allows a given compliant mechanism to be scaled to a desired natural frequency. The comparison of the results obtained with CaTEf and those obtained with FEM in terms of the scaling factor and the natural frequencies shows only slight deviations and makes a big difference in the modeling and computation time in favor of CaTEf. A very efficient calculation method has been successfully developed for the optimization of given compliant mechanisms with respect to their dynamic behavior, more precisely their natural frequencies. This method allows an existing design of these mechanisms to be optimized while maintaining the overall structure, and ensuring that the desired natural frequency is met for the specific requirements of the application.

articleTitle: Mechanical Design and Fluid Dynamics Simulation of a Reconfigurable Hybrid Aerial Underwater Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: In this paper, based on the fixed-wing vehicle and the autonomous underwater vehicle, we design a new hybrid aerial underwater vehicle. We are able to fold and deploy the front wings in a very short period of time by a single electric actuator. Then, we consider the aerodynamic characteristics of each wing type and determine all of the wing types. Finally, we conduct computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation of the aerial state of the vehicle to verify the feasibility and stability of aerial flight and underwater submergence of the vehicle.

articleTitle: Scale Optimization of the 7SPS Parallel Mechanism with Fewer Active Inputs than the DOFs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper delves into the motion principles of the 7SPS parallel mechanism with fewer active inputs than the DOF, thoroughly analyzing the velocity mapping relationship and motion/force transmission performance of its active and passive limbs. Building upon theoretical research, the paper further conducts scale optimization of the mechanism based on the velocity mapping and motion/force transmission performance, aiming to enhance its overall motion efficiency and mechanical transmission effect. Through this series of research and optimization, the paper provides a solid theoretical foundation and practical guidance for the prototype design of the 7SPS parallel mechanism, promising to propel technological advancements and application expansion in this field.

articleTitle: Short Inter-Robot Distance Following Based on Collision-Free Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Self-reconfigurable robots aim to develop intelli-gent robotic systems with shape variability and task adaptability. This technology employs modular design, allowing robots to autonomously adjust their shape and structure according to specific tasks. For multiple self-reconfigurable robots using mecanum wheels as their mobile platform, a collision-free nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) method is adopted to provide control strategies, enabling them to accomplish short-distance tracking tasks in real-time environments. An external radar module is utilized for global robot localization and obtaining high-precision pose information. Experiments conducted in a 3D simulation environment validate the effectiveness of this approach. In practical applications, overcoming various challenges such as hardware design, communication, and perception is essential to achieve robustness and reliability in self-reconfigurable robot systems.

articleTitle: Design, Mobility and Kinematic Analysis of a 4-DOF 3R1T Redundantly Actuated Foldable Parallel Manipulator with a Circular Rail
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The study presents a novel four-degrees-of-freedom (4-DOF) parallel manipulator with a circular rail and analyzes its mobility and kinematics. The manipulator has three rotational and one translational DOFs (a 3R1T motion pattern), where the center of spherical motion translates along the rail axis. The innovative design of the manipulator makes it possible to fold between spatial and planar configurations. The circular rail provides the manipulator with unlimited rotation about the rail axis. Two redundant drives make the manipulator design symmetrical, equalizing load distribution between three kinematic chains. Screw theory confirms the motion pattern and proper actuation scheme of the manipulator. Kinematic analysis presents a closed-form solution to the inverse kinematic problem. Numerical examples simulated in the MATLAB package verify the theoretical computations.

articleTitle: Compliant Spherical Joint Design for Reconfiguration of Variable Topology Truss
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compliant spherical joint for the Variable Topology Truss (VTT) system that enables topology self-reconfiguration. Self-reconfiguration is a common feature of modular robot systems. In a truss-type modular system, self-reconfiguration requires care to prevent collapse and control truss position for docking. This paper proposes maintaining structure stability while disconnecting truss members during reconfiguration by adding joint stiffness between members. Keeping the members in equilibrium allows predictive positioning to aid reconfiguration. In this study, we present the self-reconfiguration of a tetrahedral VTT system as a simple demonstration. The required stiffness value for the spherical joint mechanism was calculated by statics simulation. A joint and docking prototype is demonstrated with docking to show the feasibility of this proposed self-reconfiguration procedure.

articleTitle: Configuration Innovation and Stability Analysis of a Hexapod Load-bearing Mountain Climbing Robot XuanGui
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: A hexapod mountain climbing robot that can carrying heavy objects based on 2-UPU&2-RPR parallel mechanism, named XuanGui, is presented. 2-UPU&2-RPR redundant parallel mechanism can ensure the horizontal orientation of the platforms during motion through an inline parallelogram configuration. Connecting the upper platform and the loading platform with the revolute pair can enable the robot to have zero radius flexible turning ability. The extended structure of its landing foot-end can have good passing ability in muddy terrain. The gait of the XuanGui robot is designed. The stability of the XuanGui robot is analyzed. The XuanGui robot can be used to carry heavy objects instead of porters in famous mountain scenic areas.

articleTitle: Motion Mode Analysis of a Variable-DOF 8R Spatial Mechanism Composed of Four Plane Symmetric RRR Triads
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Current research on variable-DOF (or kinema-totropic) single-loop spatial mechanisms is mainly about single-loop 7R mechanisms. This paper is about the motion mode analysis of a variable-DOF single-loop 8R spatial mechanism, which is composed of four (identical) plane symmetric RRR triads. Firstly, a description of the variable-DOF single-loop 8R spatial mechanism is given. A set of kinematic loop equations is then formulated using dual quaternions and the natural exponential function substitution. All the motion modes of the 8R mechanism are obtained by solving the set of equations using prime decomposition of ideals. The analysis shows that the variable-DOF single-loop 8R spatial mechanism has six motion modes, including four 3-DOF modes and two 2-DOF plane/line symmetric modes. This work provides a solid foundation for the reconfiguration analysis of other multi-mode single-loop 8R mechanisms and multi-loop mechanisms involving multi-mode single-loop 8R mechanisms.

articleTitle: Configuration Change and Kinematics Analysis of a Novel Reconfigurable Parallel Mechanism with Metamorphic Joint
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper introduces the TS joint, a new type of metamorphic joint derived from the conventional Hooke joint. By performing locking devices and aligning the rotational axes, the TS joint has both physical and geometric ways of metamorphosis, resulting in eight typical phases ranging from three to one rotational degree of freedom (DOF). By utilizing TS joints, a (TS)P(TS) reconfigurable limb is constructed and the constraints of distinct phases of the limb are analyzed based on the principles of the screw theory. A novel 3(TS)P(TS) reconfigurable parallel mechanism (RPM) is constructed, featuring three (TS)P(TS) reconfigurable limbs that connect the base and the platform. The constraint analysis of different configurations illustrates that the RPM achieves reconstruction among eight alternative working modes from mobility six to mobility one. Taking (TS-1)P(TS-1) and (TS-7)P(TS-1) phases of the (TS)P(TS) reconfigurable limb as an example, the unified kinematics model is established by considering one phase as a specific instance of the other. The inverse kinematics solutions covering four configurations of the RPM are acquired, and mathematical examples are provided to demonstrate the precision of the theoretical analysis. The metamorphic joint presented in this paper expands the sorts of RPMs, and the kinematics analysis lays a solid foundation for the singularity and workspace analysis of novel RPMs.

articleTitle: A Geometric Approach for the Bifurcation Modeling and Analysis of Plane-Symmetric Bricard Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: As a classical type of overconstrained linkages, the spatial 6R single-loop Bricard mechanisms have long attracted researchers' attention. In our previous work, a comprehensive geometric approach is established for the kinematics analysis of general plane-symmetric Bricard mechanisms, with an intuitive interpretation of kinematic properties. In this paper, this novel approach is further extended for the bifurcation analysis of the plane-symmetric Bricard mechanisms. Owing to the geometric representation, the condition of bifurcations can be interpreted as a continuous intersection of two coplanar ellipses, including their degeneration. All possible scenarios are analyzed in detail, based on which the corresponding kinematic conditions can be specified to distinguish Bricard mechanisms with bifurcations. A comprehensive categorization is provided to classify the can-didates into different categories according to various conditions. Case studies are made to enumerate all categories of kinematic bifurcations, in an intuitive way, with the geometric illustration of mobility in these special configurations.

articleTitle: An Efficient Design Model for Parallel-Guided Layer Jamming Compliant Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Layer jamming (LJ) materials and structures have shown promise in designing variable stiffness compliant mechanisms for robotics. However, design challenges persist due to time-consuming prototyping, testing, and significant compu-tational resources needed for finite element (FE) simulations. The complexity stems from the intricate mechanics behavior between jamming materials and substrate structures. This article presents a hybrid model that combines machine learning (ML) with data generated from finite element (FE) analysis to predict the mechanical behavior of LJ -based compliant parallel-guided mechanisms, including force-deflection relationships, stiffness, and hysteresis. An experimentally validated FE model generates data by varying geometric and material parameters, capturing key mechanical performance metrics. This data serves as input for training a neural network model, which evaluates the impact of selected design parameters on performance metrics. The resulting ML model is highly efficient, with predictions taking seconds compared to hundreds of hours needed for FE simulations, and remarkably accurate, with less than a 5% error relative to FE simulations. This efficient computational model can be used for designing and analyzing LJ-based parallel-guided mechanisms, with the validated workflow process applicable to other LJ -compliant mechanisms and robotic systems.

articleTitle: Kinetic-Geometric Synthesis of a Reconfigurable 4R Four-bar Multitask Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper proposes a design of a reconfigurable force balanced planar 4R four-bar linkage that can be applied for a variety of three-position motion tasks. Based on given and fixed link lengths of the four-bar linkage, from three-position synthesis the locations of the coupler pivots and base pivots can be derived for a desired set of three poses. With respect to the end-effector at the coupler link the two coupler pivots can be reconfigured in a balanced way with balanced five-bar parallelogram linkages such that force balance of the complete linkage is maintained at any time. Similarly the two base pivots can be reconfigured in a balanced way with balanced five-bar parallelogram linkages such that force balance of the complete mechanism is maintained for motion of the end-effector through any chosen set of three poses. The balance conditions for the complete mechanism are derived step by step with mass equivalent models.

articleTitle: A Novel Analytical Method for Path Synthesis of Spherical Four-Bar Mechanism Based on Fourier Series
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: In this paper, a novel analytical approach for synthesizing a path-generation mechanism of spherical four-bar mechanism without any limitation on the number of precision points is presented. Compared with classical analytical methods, the novelty of the proposed method is that the synthesis equations were established based on the relationship between the design variables and the Fourier coefficients of the path instead of the displacement matrix. Based on the presented synthesis equations, the path generation problem of spherical four-bar linkages was reduced to solving two polynomial equations of low complexity. Moreover, a general formula was derived from the analytical solutions of the new synthesis equations, where the design variables could be directly calculated with the Fourier coefficients of the prescribed path. An example is provided to evaluate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method. The findings indicate that the proposed method is simple, efficient, and readily programmed.

articleTitle: Shared Workspace and Cable Interference Between Point-Mass Cable-Driven Parallel Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This article presents an analytical method for geometrically determining the interference-free workspaces of multiple point-mass cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) sharing a common space. The method presents different types of cable interference and introduces the concept of the shortest path to interference to directly identify the cable interference configurations closest to the initial configurations of each point-mass CDPR. This makes it possible to determine an independent interference-free ellipsoidal workspace for each robot.

articleTitle: CAD-Based Workspace Analysis of a 6-DOF Foldable Parallel Manipulator with a Circular Rail (FoldRail Manipulator)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Nowadays, computer-aided design (CAD) finds many applications in the development and analysis of manipulators and robots. It accurately reflects the design features of the considered mechanical system, including the geometry and material of its links. This article applies CAD tools to analyze a workspace of a 6-DOF foldable parallel manipulator with a circular rail (FoldRail manipulator). The article proposes an algorithm to determine a translation (constant orientation) workspace of the manipulator using a geometrical method implemented in the SolidWorks software. The combination of this method and a CAD model of the manipulator allows considering all of its design features. The results are presented for the horizontal and tilted orientations of the output link.

articleTitle: Hybrid Locomotion of a Mobile Parallel Robot with a Minimal Number of Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents several novel designs of hybrid locomotion for a mobile parallel robot. With the proposed hybrid locomotion, the robot can move by walking or on wheels. The novelty of the proposal is offering dual locomotion without adding more motors. This is achieved by introducing a switching clutch that can transmit the motor rotation to either the walking mechanism or the wheels. Two designs are proposed, namely: 1) hybrid locomotion with omnidirectional wheels and 2) hybrid locomotion with steered standard wheels. The latter design consists of two schemes: one with suction and another without suction. Each of the schemes may have one of four possible wheel configurations. Without adding more motors, a set of solenoids is required to activate the switching clutches, and additional transmission modules are needed to transmit the motors' rotation to the wheels. The use of a switching mechanism leads to a significantly suppressed cost of the robot as the main motors are much more expensive than the solenoids and the additional transmission components. The details of each design were presented in the paper, followed by a comparison between them. One may choose any of the designs depending on the requirements and needs. Furthermore, one may implement all the designs by exchanging the wheel assembly and its switching mechanism due to the modularity.

articleTitle: Design of High Efficiency Bio-Inspired Hydraulic Actuator for Wearable Robotic System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Inefficiency is a technical bottleneck that affects the widespread use of wearable robots. Inspired by the efficient motor mechanism of human muscles, we designed a high efficiency Bio-inspired Hydraulic Actuator (BHA) that combines pump, cylinder, valve and motor in a compact structure. By mimicking the structure of the multi-fiber motor unit and the power supply mode of human muscles, the new actuator adopts a two-stage energy supply mode and an innovative structure of two pumps and two cylinders. Through such a design, the output power and force of the BHA can precisely match the change of load, reducing the throttling loss in the traditional hydraulic system and greatly improving the system efficiency of the bionic wearable robot. The analysis and experiments in this paper show that the actuator of the integrated pump cylinder has good energy efficiency, and the prosthesis using BHA can achieve a gait consistent with human normal walking.

articleTitle: Kinematics and Configuration Analysis of a Five-Fingered Metamorphic Robot Hand
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This research presents a novel metamorphic multi-fingered robotic hand, characterized by its innovative reconfigurable palm structure. The robotic hand's distinctive design incorporates a closed-loop series palm structure in conjunction with bilaterally movable fingers, markedly augmenting its orientation and pose flexibility. This enhancement substantially broadens the operational workspace of the robotic fingers. The paper initially details the structure of the Metamorphic hand, comprising an articulated palm and five fingers. It delves into the design parameters of the Metamorphic hand's hybrid structure and unveils analytical models for both forward and inverse kinematics. These models facilitate the determination of the reachable workspace and the trajectories of all five fingertips. To further explore this expanded workspace, the study introduces the concept of finger orientation planes, linking finger orientation to various palm configurations. To illustrate the relationship between finger-orientation planes and hand posture, a four-dimensional Gauss map is employed. Sub-sequently, manifolds representing finger orientation, varying based on hand pose, are derived from the ruled surface. The paper also includes workspace simulations that demonstrate the unique capabilities and dexterity of this novel robotic hand, highlighting its potential applications and advancements in robotic manipulation.

articleTitle: A low rotational inertia reconfigurable 3D thrust vector leg mechanism for legged robot capable of omnidirectional legged locomotion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The structure design of the robotic leg is a core and hot research area for legged robots. In this paper, we report a series-parallel reconfigurable 3D thrust vector leg mechanism with 3 degree-of-freedom (DOF). Upper leg is a spatial dual-parallelogram-linkages parallel mechanism, lower leg is a spatial closed-loop eight-bar mechanism. The kinematic model of the mechanism is built based on the screw theory, and the mechanism's control complexity is examined and contrasted. The kinematic performance and static performance of the leg mechanism are analyzed. A quadruped robot is built based on the proposed leg mechanism., and the omnidirectional legged locomotion is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Single-Loop Multiple Metamorphic Mechanism Inspired by Thick-Panel Origami
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The relationship between origami and mechanism is very close, and the construction theory of thick-panel origami contains the way to discover new mechanism. There are relatively few single-loop metamorphic mechanisms generated from thick-panel origami. Inspired by thick-panel origami derived from Miura origami, this paper proposes a novel single-loop 6R multiple metamorphic mechanism. By constructing and solving the D-H closed-loop equation of the mechanism and analyzing its singular configuration by using the screw theory, the planar, spherical and Bennett motion branches of the mechanism are illustrated and all the three bifurcation points between motion branches are given.

articleTitle: A Bionic Morphing Tail Mechanism for Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Aerial vehicles, inspired by birds, provide a promising platform for effective winged flight and environmental interaction. However, these vehicles still face challenges when navigating complex, obstacle-rich environments. At present, the flight control of aerial vehicles is primarily managed by the tail. However, most ornithopters typically feature a tail with one or two degrees of freedom (DoFs), significantly limiting the maneuverability and agility of the vehicles. In response to this limitation, our research introduces a bionic bird-inspired morphing tail mechanism with four DoFs related to tilt, elevation, and rudder. We present the design, analysis, simulation, and prototyping of this morphing mechanism. In biology, this robot serves as a valuable tool to explore how birds utilize their tails for dynamic maneuvers and fly more efficiently. In robotics, our creation becomes a testbed for exploring vertical tail-less flight and the control of morphing surfaces.

articleTitle: Implementation of Coordinated Circular Motion for Two Mobile Robots Based on Safe Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Traditional ground mobile robots have been widely used in various scenarios. However, the complex environment and its own mechanical structure make its movement limited. Based on the traditional Dubins car model, this article constructs multiple Dubins car collaborative motion models. We use the control Lyapunov function, control barrier function, and quadratic programming (CLF-CBF-QP) to design corresponding control constraints for different stages of the collaborative motion. This can ensure the self-reconstruction characteristics of the collaborative motion. Meanwhile, we conduct simulation experiments to verify the feasibility of the CLF -CBF -QP control algorithm for collaborative motion control.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Optimization of Contact-Aided Compliant Mechanisms with Prescribed Nonlinear Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple synthesis method of the beam-based contact-aided compliant mechanisms (CCMs) based on the chained pseudo-rigid-body model (CPRBM). The proposed method can be applied under any loading conditions and provide an alternative design tool to the finite element analysis (FEA). Then, a concise optimization framework is presented, followed by two numerical examples to validate the feasibility of the proposed method. Polynomial curves are used to describe the profile of contact surfaces. The analysis results verify the accuracy of the analytical model and demonstrate that the proposed method can be used to obtain the CCMs with desired functionalities, e.g., nonlinear force-displacement characteristic and minimum average center drift. Finally, the limitations of this paper and some outlooks are discussed. Furthermore, the proposed method retains the generality in shape and dimension and can be extended for the synthesis of general beams and arbitrary contact surfaces.

articleTitle: Resampling Strategies for Increasing Point Density in Narrow Passages for Probabilistic Roadmaps
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents multiple point-sampling strategies for stochastic approach to path planning. Their main purpose is to increase points density in narrow corridors, which are often difficult areas to navigate using non-deterministic approach for path planning. At the same time, algorithms for distributing points over the area of narrow regions and reducing their number in open space are described as well as postprocessing algorithm distancing samples from obstacles. Simulation-based tests are performed to compare achieved results and estimate calculation times.

articleTitle: Type Synthesis of Single-DOF Multi-Loop-Coupled Planar Continuum Morphing Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper investigates a single degree-of-freedom (DOF) multi-loop-coupled planar continuum morphing mechanism (MPCMM), which can be used in broad application prospects in fields such as robotics, aerospace, and biomedical devices. The mechanism is proposed based on the generalized kinematic chains. The design process mainly includes determining the design requirements, selecting the generalized kinematic chains based on the design requirements, modifying the chains, and choosing the most appropriate chain to construct MPCMM. In addition, the vector equation method is used to analyze the mechanisms. Finally, the MPCMM is applied to a variable camber wing trailing edge.

articleTitle: Enumerating Deformed Configurations of Reconfigurable Meshed Cellular Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Reconfigurable meshed cellular robots could be the future of next-generation adaptive structures and robots as they can undergo large shape changes while simultaneously bearing loads. This paper considers an embodiment of meshed cellular robots as a network combination of several Soft Two-State building blocks that can either be stiff or actuate like a muscle. Given a target deformed shape, it is required to determine the morphological state of each building block in the network (a stiff bone or a contractile muscle) that maximally meets the shape. The paper presents techniques to reduce the design space of possibilities by specifically isolating a bio-inspired two-muscle one-bone pattern for each triangular mesh. Enumeration of all designs that meet this pattern is shown to maximally capture all large deformation shapes. This significantly simplifies computations required for design evaluations and control with several design alternatives pre-sented to the designer. An example of an aquatic fin is used to illustrate the methodology where all prominent deformation modes of the fin can be captured through the pattern-based enumeration scheme. Future work can expand this methodology by considering more patterns and embedding the enumeration scheme within a generative topology design framework.

articleTitle: Mobility, Singularity and Configuration Analysis of a Bennett-Based Reconfigurable 8R Linkage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable spatial 8R linkage is discussed. By adding coaxial joints to the links of a Bennett linkage, the mechanism is allowed to switch between a series of Bennett linkages with the same rod-length ratio and continuous different twist angles. Two types of revolute joints, which are θ-joint and a-joint, have been defined. Kinematic model of the mechanism is established based on the screw theory, whereby a singularity and mobility criterion in intuitive form is proposed and applied. Due to the 2 DoFs of the reconfigurable 8R linkage, the mechanism is able to both fold around its diagonal and change the twist angles of the θ-joint axes. The relationship of the two DoFs is developed, which explains the decoupled folding and twisting action of the mechanism. Simulations and prototype testing have been performed to validate the analysis. In the end, a series of derivative mechanisms, which have the same movement but different kinematic pairs, are presented.

articleTitle: Design of a Torque-Resistant Continuum Origami Robot Module with Embedded Frame
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Continuum robots offer unique capabilities for various applications, while their performance can be limited by the external forces experienced during actuation. In this work, we present an origami actuator designed as a continuum robot module, featuring an embedded frame with a magnetic ball joint. The embedded frame enhances the actuator's resistance to external forces, while the magnetic ball joint prevents forced bending in the opposite direction when a load is applied, addressing a common challenge in continuum robot design. We describe the design, fabrication process, and mechanical anal-ysis of the actuator, demonstrating its improved performance compared to traditional designs. Experimental results show that the actuator equipped with our embedded frame exhibits higher resistance to external forces, making it potential for applications requiring robust actuation.

articleTitle: Thrust-velocity Characteristics of a Variable Composite Wave Driven Bionic Undulating Propeller
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Bionic undulating fin is more silent, efficient and environmental friendly than traditional underwater propulsion methods. To improve the thrust force and velocity of undulating propellers, we proposed a longitudinal and transverse composite wave propulsion method. A variable bionic undulating fin propeller with multi-degree-of-freedom is designed and developed. The mathematical model of the composite wave is established, and its wave control rule is proposed. Through computational fluid dynamics simulation, the hydrodynamic and motion performance of the undulating fin propeller under different longitudinal wave amplitudes and frequencies is compared. The simulation results show that the longitudinal and transverse composite wave can significantly improve the propulsion force and velocity of the undulating fin. The average and the peak value of thrust force can be increased by 28.5% and 200%, respectively. The experimental results of the physical prototype show that the stable velocity of the undulating fin at 2 Hz frequency and 20° longitudinal wave amplitude reaches 0.761 m/s, which is 14.7% higher than that without longitudinal wave. The research results show that the composite wave has better thrust and velocity performance than single sinusoidal transverse wave, which provides a new mechanism for high performance soft bionic fish.

articleTitle: Kinematic Analysis and Dimensional Synthesis of a Reconfigurable Parallel Mechanism for Wine Box Production Line
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: A reconfigurable parallel mechanism is proposed to automate the gluing of the wine box glue line and the scrap-clearing of the wine box base on the wine box production line. Firstly, based on the lockable joint, the mechanism can switch between 3T (T denotes translation) and 3T1R (R denotes rotation) motion modes. The closed-loop vector method and the D-H method are presented to determine the inverse position in the corresponding mode. The position inverse equation is derived to obtain the Jacobian matrix of the mechanism and its singularity is analyzed. In 3T motion mode, the dexterity index is analyzed. In 3TIR motion mode, the velocity index is analyzed. The spatial model method is used to obtain the performance map of the corresponding motion mode, and the dimension parameters are optimized according to the practical application requirements to improve the kinematic performance of the mechanism.

articleTitle: Tracking Control of Two Mobile Robots in Leader-Follower Mode Based on Terminal Sliding Mode Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: In order to solve the docking problem of multiple wheeled mobile robots in the process of motion, this paper presents a controller for the formation of wheeled mobile robot. The proposed control law provides a method for the leader agent to track the target trajectory. The follower agent keeps a given distance from the leader and follows the position and attitude of the leader to prepare for the docking task with the leader. Based on terminal sliding mode control, the proposed controller provides the finite-time convergence of the formation errors. The controllers are designed based on Lyapunov stability analysis. In conclusion, a numerical example is offered to demonstrate the practicality and usefulness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Homogeneous Module Unit Morphology Optimization and Design for On-Orbit Services
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: In order to meet the increasingly complex space missions, this paper designs a homogeneous modular unit form that can be reconfigured into single-chain, two-branch, three-branch and four-branch configurations of space robots. Through the analysis of on-orbit service tasks, the future space robot configuration needs are obtained, and the interface configuration scheme of four interfaces of the modular unit is designed; in order to ensure the motion capability and flexibility of the modular unit, six modular unit degree-of-freedom configurations are proposed, and through the comparative analysis of the motion capability and degree-of-freedom redundancy, and the performance synthesis of the single-chain configuration of the modular unit, such as the mass, degree-of-freedom, workspace and load capacity, the preferred modular unit is selected as the best configuration for the single-chain configuration. Through the comparative analysis of kinematic capability and redundancy of degrees of freedom, as well as the mass, degrees of freedom, working space and load capacity of the single-chain configuration space robot composed of the modular unit, a three-degree-of-freedom configuration scheme is preferred, including two interface degrees of freedom with variable angles and one internal degree of freedom at 45° to the interface degrees of freedom; combined with the analysis of structural load-bearing performance, the design of the sphere of the modular unit is accomplished; and finally, the interface configuration, degrees of freedom configuration and the design of the sphere is synthesized, and a homogenous Modular unit morphology.

articleTitle: Metamorphic Robotic Gripper for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper introduces a metamorphic robotic gripper for industrial applications. Pick and place operations in industry typically require two actuators; one to close and open the gripper fingers around the desired object, and another to retract or extend the object. The gripper proposed by this paper is a one degree of freedom mechanism, allowing a single gripping mechanism to both grasp an object and extend and retract the object using one actuator. The gripper operates using a variable joint that changes the representative orientation of a prismatic joint as the gripper fingers move through the desired motion profile. The advantage of this metamorphic mechanism as compared to traditional pick and place systems is that this gripper only requires one actuator. This reduction in actuators potentially lowers the mechanism's weight, reduces cost, and uses less power for the same range of motion. In this paper, the new metamorphic gripper is described, its topology analyzed using directionality topology matrices, and an initial prototype is presented showing the mechanism performing the desired grasping motion using an open loop controller. The result is a new metamorphic gripper that has potential advantages when compared to conventional solutions.

articleTitle: Cable Tension Optimization for a Planar CDPR Through Anchor Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper introduced a novel approach in Cable-Driven Parallel Robots (CDPRs) on planar surface applications. It focuses on challenges in redundancy, reconfiguration, and payload capacity. The research presents innovative solutions for cable tension optimization and anchor reconfiguration, aiming to resolve redundancy issues in multi-anchor systems. It combines theoretical models with experimental data from extensive laboratory experiments, employing linear programming to optimize cable-driven redundant parallel manipulators. This approach underlines the paper's contribution to enhancing the operational efficiency and precision of CDPRs, ensuring practical applicability of the findings.

articleTitle: A Novel Bio-Inspired Quadruped Crawling Robot with Movable Waist
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Traditional quadruped robots usually have rigid and fixed torso, which limits their mobility and flexibility. Robots with movable waist can improve the flexibility and environmental adaptability of robots. In this paper, a novel bionic crawling robot with movable waist is proposed. The movable waist innovatively adopts an anti-parallelogram mechanism. At the same time, the waist adopts a double-layer structure design to increase the stability and bearing capacity of the robot. The kinematics model of the robot is derived based on the D-H parameter method. Bas ed on the Monte Carlo method, the toe workspace of the leg is obtained in Matlab software. The results show that due to the torsion of the movable waist, the toe workspace is significantly expanded, and the robot can achieve faster and smoother motion. A prototype was made based on 3D printing technology for experimental verification.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Deployable Network Mechanism Constructed by Bricard-Like Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a novel reconfigurable deployable network mechanism constructed by Bricard-like mechanisms. The reconfigurable Bricard-like mechanism is designed by connecting three identical dual angulated elements (AEs) and spatial RRR (R denotes revolute) chains. By alternately arranging adjacent Bricard-like mechanisms in a forward and reverse configuration, a reconfigurable deployable network mechanism (RDNM) is constructed. The newly proposed RDNM has two deployable motion modes, including the scissor-like deployable mode and Bricard-like deployable mode, and these two deployable modes can be transformed by a switching configuration. Further, the degree of freedom (DOF) of RDNM in the scissor-like deployable mode is analyzed based on screw theory and kinematic characteristics of RDNM in the Bricard-like deployable mode is examined. The RDNM proposed in this paper shows the construction potential of multi-layer reconfigurable deployable network mechanism in the future.

articleTitle: Design and Kinematics Characteristics Analysis of an Extendable Arm and Deployable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Due to the spatial constraints of payload bays in ground-based space launchers, certain large-scale spaceborne devices such as solar panel, antennas and arms cannot be launched and carried in their existing ground-based configurations. This paper addresses this situation by proposing a novel deployable antenna unit. Based on the screw theory and graph theory, a topological constraint graph for the deployable unit is established. Kinematic analysis and a simulation model for the deployable unit is developed to validate the correctness of the degree of freedom theoretical analysis. We conducted a novel space deployable antenna based on the deployable unit, and the simulation results indicate their deployability.

articleTitle: Research on Attitude and Control of a Bionic Manta Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The bionic manta robot intertwines two contemporary areas of interest: biomimetics and sub aquatic robotics. Drawing insights from a proposed bionic manta robot, this research analyzes the motion attitude of the robot and establishes the relevant parameters. In order to achieve the smooth gait switching of the robot, a CPG controller based on Hopf oscillator is applied in this paper, and the impact of different parameters on the robot motion is studied. Ultimately, the prototype of the robot is crafted and the motion attitude is validated through pool experiments, showcasing its impressive performance capabilities.

articleTitle: Tri-Sphero Bot: A Modular Compliant Unit with Spherical Wheels
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Modular robots offer promising applications in fields like swarm robotics and exploration, and have been extensively explored in the academic research. Specifically, some soft robots, even with the complex system dynamics, exhibit their usefulness in tasks involving navigation of unfamiliar environments. In this study, we present a compliant robot design and analyze two-dimensional motion with simulation using various reference trajectories. Subsequently, we validate the optimized simulation parameters on physical hardware, revealing promising potential for effective robot control.

articleTitle: A 6R Metamorphic Mechanism with a Novel Variable-Axis Joint
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a 6R metamorphic mechanism with a novel variable-axis joint, which can achieve compliant switching between motion branches. This paper involves the utilization of a self-coupling variable-axis joint to increase the degree of freedom of the metamorphic mechanism in the vicinity of the bifurcation point. The expansion from the bifurcation point to the bifurcation domains facilitates the switching of motion branches without traversing the bifurcation point. The results show that this variable-axis joint can achieve compliant switching and also enable the mechanism to autonomously converge to the regular motion branch. The findings confirmed the feasibility and efficacy of the proposed method for achieving compliant switching between metamorphic mechanism motion branches.

articleTitle: Application of Mechanisms to Aircraft Flexible Trailing Edge Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a new design for a swept aircraft flexible trailing edge based on two new mechanism concepts. The first concept is the continuum parallel mechanism, where the top and bottom skin of a trailing edge are treated as two moving branches that are connected to the trailing edge tip to morph an airfoil shape. The second concept is the auxetic structure that resembles a compliant mechanism, based on which a set of morphing ribs were investigated to accommodate airfoil shape morphing. To facilitate the design of a swept flexible trailing edge, finite element models were developed to analyze required shape morphing without skin twisting. Several auxetic structures were evaluated, from which a bow-tie structure was selected for integration with a flexible trailing edge. Finally, a swept flexible trailing edge was built and integrated with a full-size winglet. The test results have demonstrated that the proposed design is effective in providing the required morphing motion and sustaining the required load.

articleTitle: Kinematics, Singularity and Workspace Analysis of a Reconfigurable Parallel Mechanism for Large Scale Assembly
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Reconfigurable parallel mechanisms (RPMs) own the advantages of high stiffness., good dynamic performance due to their parallel structural features., and can reconfigure themselves to accommodate different., complicated and changeable task requirements. This paper deals with kinematics of an RPM which can be converted into three operation modes in six motion cases. First., inverse kinematic models of the RPM are established through the method of closed-loop vector. Then Jacobian matrices of the RPM are derived., based on which singularity of the system can be analyzed. Finally., reachable workspace of the RPM is searched by considering corresponding constraint conditions. Results show that workspace of RPM is continuous and there is no empty hole. However., singularities occur in the reachable workspace, which should be avoided in trajectory planning.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Origami-Based Vibration Isolators with High-Static-Low-Dynamic-Stiffness Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper focuses on the structure, dynamics, and isolation performance of the proposed two-stage high-static-low-dynamic-stiffness (HSLDS) vibration isolator consisting of two Tachi-Miura origami units in series. Torsion springs are placed at creases to introduce elastic effect into the origami-based vibration isolator. Employing the nonlinear stiffness properties of Tachi-Miura origami, the HSLDS characteristics of the isolator unit are achieved by adjusting the stiffness coefficient of the spring at the creases. Moreover, an equivalent dynamic model of the coupled origami-based isolator is established; the analytical steady-state behavior is obtained. The force trans-missibility results and comparative analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of the presented two-stage origami-based isolator in low-frequency vibration isolation.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Spatial Parasitic Compensation Mechanisms Supporting Triaxial Compliant Positioning Stages
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Compliant mechanisms have become state-of-the-art solutions for designing high-precision mechanisms, free from issues like friction wear, backlash, and the need for lubrication. These advantages are critical for applications in ultraclean or harsh environments, although they come with the drawback of parasitic deflection. This work introduces a flexure-based mechanism that compensates for spatial parasitic motion and can be utilized in triaxial compliant positioning stages. The overconstrained symmetric configuration in this design improves spatial precise motion, enhancing stiffness and accuracy. Additionally, a theoretical stiffness model is established to characterize the mechanical performance of the spatial compliant mechanism. Finite element analysis (FEA) is then conducted to investigate the motion behavior of the triaxial compliant positioning stages. The results demonstrate significant potential for applications such as nanoimprint lithography (NIL) that require three-dimensional precision pointing, positioning, and alignment of terminal actuators.

articleTitle: Kinematic Calibration for a Large Hybrid Spraying Robot Considering Gravity Deformation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: For large robot, gravity deformation has an impact on the calibration of kinematic parameters. This paper proposes a kinematic parameter calibration method considering gravity deformation for a large hybrid spraying robot. Firstly, the kinematic error model of the hybrid robot is formulated by combining the error models of the main serial chain and the parallelogram mechanism through passive joint angle. Then the stiffness model of the hybrid robot is established by combining finite element method and matrix structural analysis. Finally, a kinematic parameter calibration method considering gravity deformation is proposed. The effectiveness of the accuracy compensation strategy proposed is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Dynamic Characteristics Analysis of the 3-(PRPR)RS Parallel Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: A three-degree-of-freedom 3-2(Prismatic-Revolute)-Revolute-Spherical (3-(PRPR)RS) parallel manipulator is proposed where its kinematics and dynamics characteristics are studied. First, the kinematic characteristics of the structure of 3-(PRPR)RS parallel manipulator are analyzed, and the constraint relation and inverse kinematics equations of each branch chain of the manipulator are deduced. Second, by analyzing the kinetic energy and potential energy of 3-(PRPR)RS parallel manipulator, the analytical dynamic equation of the 3-(PRPR)RS parallel manipulator is derived from the Lagrange equation. Third, the kinematic characteristics of the 3-(PRPR)RS parallel manipulator and the system's dynamic characteristics such as driving force and energy consumption are discussed using a numerical example. The research content provides a theoretical basis for deeply understanding the dynamic essence of the 3-(PRPR)RS parallel manipulator, and further developing the performance optimization and high-precision control of the 3-(PRPR)RS parallel manipulator.

articleTitle: Virtualized Digital Twin (DT) of a Reconfigurable Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of digital twin technology and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) within the scope of industrial automation, emphasizing the transformative potential of these technologies in enhancing the efficiency and functionality of PLCs. By leveraging the capabilities of OpenPLC—an open-source software—this research aims to demonstrate the significant advancements in automation practices that can be achieved by simulating PLC systems virtually. This approach not only promises more reliable and cost-effective automation solutions but also significantly improves design and operational effectiveness, thus marking a significant leap forward in the automation domain. Central to our study is the integration of digital twin technology, which facilitates the real-time simulation, analysis, and optimization of automated systems, thereby reducing costs and commissioning times. The paper also highlights the adoption of fully open-source software to address the scalability of inputs and outputs in automation systems, overcoming the limitations imposed by physical hardware. Our methodology utilizes the OpenPLC runtime deployed within a Docker container to ensure scalable and efficient system deployment. Furthermore, the system setup incorporates MQTT for efficient data transmission and a custom Python script to facilitate communication between virtual and physical PLCs through MQTT and MODBUS protocols. Uniquely, this research offers a groundbreaking perspective by combining the robustness of open-source tools with the precision of digital twins, paving the way for future innovations in automated control systems and setting a new benchmark for open, scalable, and highly efficient industrial automation frameworks.

articleTitle: Motion Control of a Cable-Driven Parallel Robot Using Reinforcement Learning Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Multi - Agent
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Machine learning has demonstrated a great capacity to find solutions for various research in the control and robotic realm. Reinforcement learning is a branch of machine learning which can interact with the environment while searching for desirable scenarios and eliminating the undesirable ones in controlling the robot. Though many studies have shown the significant performance of machine learning over the classic control methods, there are many unexplored strategies for improving the performance of the overall controller in machine learning, especially reinforcement learning. This paper provides a case study on the efficient control of a cable-driven parallel robot using the deep deterministic policy gradient multiagent and the possibility of transfer learning in this context.

articleTitle: A Novel Morphing Quadrotor UAV with Sarrus-Linkage-Based Reconfigurable Frame
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Nature provides a repertoire of flyers demonstrating dynamic maneuvering during flight by effectively using their morphological changes, thus adapting to environmental variability. However, most conventional multirotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) use rigid and single-configuration platforms, limiting their adaptability to environment and task changes. To address this limitation, this work proposes a novel morphing quadrotor UAV with a reconfigurable frame capable of changing its size during flight. The reconfigurable frame integrates two coplanar parallelogram four-bar linkages into each limb of a four-sided Sarrus linkage. This leads to a single degree of freedom (DoF) parallel mechanism with a symmetric structure, which ensures the four motor arms are coplanar and always with the same length while the morphing quadrotor UAV size changes. Based on this design, we investigate the feasibility of the morphing quadrotor UAV by building a proof-of-concept prototype that can change its size from a maximum of 410 mm to a minimum of 310 mm, meaning it can reduce the size by 24.4% and actively adapt to changing environment during flight. The in-flight morphing test shows that the morphing quadrotor UAV can implement a stable flight at various sizes. The experimental tests also demonstrate the potential for deploying the morphing quadrotor UAV in applications where the robot needs to navigate through narrow openings.

articleTitle: Flexible Wing Dynamics of an Underwater Gliding Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Biological flapping wing propulsion is known for its high efficiency, high mobility and high stability. The pectoral fins of fish contains nerves, muscle contraction, power transmission, biomaterials, etc., providing thrust and steering to the fish. Many scholars have studied the physiology and ecology of fish fins. Investigations have shown that the structure and size of the pectoral fins have an important influence on the swimming performance of fish, and also the flapping wing robots. This paper designed a special underwater gliding robot, manta-ray inspired robot, analyzed the motion mechanism of the flapping wing propulsion, designed a new flexible wing propulsion device - tensegrity structure, and used the Euler-Lagrange equation to establish its dynamics model, and derived the static stiffness of the tensegrity structure. The cycle variation rules of the fluid force applied to the system and the tension applied to the structure were obtained through MATLAB. A prototype was fabricated, and the feasibility of the flexible wing mounted on a manta-ray inspired robot was verified through tests.

articleTitle: Sensor Fusion-Based Parameterized Curve-Driven Modeling for Digital Twin of Reconfigurable Soft Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Soft robotics, driven by material and design advancements, presents challenges for visualization and simulation due to its complex deformations. This paper proposes a digital twin (DT) system for reconfigurable soft robots in augmented reality (AR) environments. Leveraging parameterized curve-driven methods, the system enables dynamic modification of digital twins, accurately representing deformations. Three primary deformation patterns are identified, and sensor fusion captures real-time structural changes. Implemented within an AR environment, the system allows immersive inspection and simulation of soft robots. A case study validates its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Tension Optimization of a Cable-Driven Robot by Screw Statics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for the allocation of cable force within an over-constrained eight-cable-driven robot. The structure configuration of the robot is introduced with an emphasis of over constraint characteristics. Then, the inverse kinematics of robots is carried out to address the cable length variations. Subsequently, the screw statics is employed to establish the inner force analysis model of the robot. By imposing specific boundary constraints, the tension distribution issue is transformed into an optimization problem. To avoid the virtual tension problem of cables inherent in conventional optimization methods, the proposed method introduces preloaded tension within the cables. The optimization problem is solved by using Lagrange multipliers, and the procedure for resolving tension within the cable system under varying multiplier constraints is discussed. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through numerical experiments, indicating its capacity to solve optimization of cable-driven over-constrained robot by screw statics.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Superelastic Compliant Mechanisms for Target Shape Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The design freedom of the additive manufacturing (AM) process has created new avenues for compliant mechanisms to have more complex geometries, functionality, and mechanical behavior than conventional manufacturing methods offer. However, the challenge in the assumption of “free complexity” in AM is the trial-and-error often involved in creating a design that behaves as intended. To address this problem, a synthesis method incorporating nonlinear-elastic materials and large deformations as geometric nonlinearity is proposed, using an assembly of building blocks to construct a compliant mechanism. Designs generated by the model illustrate the optimization of the building block selection, size, shape, and topology to achieve different deflected states. The combination of the superelastic behavior of shape memory alloys such as Nitinol, and the exploration of different building block geometries, has been shown to enhance the flexibility of the optimized mechanism to reach such target shapes.

articleTitle: The Surrogate Fold Catalog: a Design Tool for Origami-Inspired Mechanical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Origami has inspired work in many fields of science and engineering. However, it can be difficult to transfer the motion of an origami design from folded paper to thicker, stiffer materials. When using engineering materials, creases from an origami fold pattern are usually replaced with “surrogate folds”. While many different surrogate folds have been developed, it is challenging for a designer to quickly survey and compare potential surrogate folds. Surrogate folds can improve many origami-inspired designs and applications by changing how the designs are manufactured and how they behave. This work categorizes compliant mechanisms that may be effective as surrogate folds in a large number of origami applications. This Surrogate Fold Catalog is a tool for designers of origami systems to select and/or design mechanisms that can imitate folds. Principles and characteristics are discussed that a designer should consider to design dynamic origami systems that more effectively meet design requirements, including manufacturing considerations; controlling and utilizing off-axis motion; and introducing secondary functions surrogate folds may play be-yond attaching panels together. Also presented are guidelines on how to use the Surrogate Fold Catalog to design new or adapt existing surrogate fold mechanisms by parameterizing aspects of material and geometry.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration of Modular Hyper-Redundant Manipulators via Normalised Manipulability, Workspace Density, and Workspace Volume Percentage Indices
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)

authors.preferredName: Lorenzo De Mari Casareto Dal Verme

abstract: In recent decades, the demand for service robotics has increased in different applications. In particular, inspection and maintenance tasks require to operate in hazardous, dan-gerous, or inaccessible areas where robots can safely operate. In this context, thanks to their ability to move in hazardous and constrained environments, hyper-redundant manipulators represent an effective solution. Typically, the design of specific devices is required to accomplish inspection and maintenance tasks. Thus, changes in the working environment imply the necessity of designing new customised devices, increasing the production cost and time. A possible solution is to design a reconfigurable hyper-redundant manipulator that can adapt its structure to have high performance in different tasks. This paper proposes a novel method to find the assembly configuration of a modular hyper-redundant manipulator exploiting the Normalised Manipulability, Workspace Density, and Workspace Volume percentage indices. The proposed algorithm performs a multi-variable analysis based on these indices to select the non-dominated assembly configurations to perform a desired task. The proposed algorithm is implemented using an exemplary modular reconfigurable hyper-redundant manipulator to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Force-EvT: A Closer Look at Robotic Gripper Force Measurement with Event-Based Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Robotic grippers are receiving increasing attention in various industries as essential components of robots for interacting and manipulating objects. While significant progress has been made in the past, conventional rigid grippers still have limitations in handling irregular objects and can damage fragile objects. We have shown that soft grippers offer deformability to adapt to a variety of object shapes and maximize object protection. At the same time, dynamic vision sensors (e.g., event-based cameras) are capable of capturing small changes in brightness and streaming them asynchronously as events, unlike RGB cameras, which do not perform well in low-light and fast-moving environments. In this paper, a dynamic-vision-based algorithm is proposed to measure the force applied to the gripper. In particular, we first set up a DVXplorer Lite series event camera to capture twenty-five sets of event data. Second, motivated by the impressive performance of the Vision Transformer (ViT) algorithm in dense image prediction tasks, we propose a new approach that demonstrates the potential for force estimation and meets the requirements of real-world scenarios. We extensively evaluate the proposed algorithm on a wide range of scenarios and settings, and show that it consistently outperforms recent approaches.

articleTitle: Design and Prototyping of a Cable-Driven Parallel Robot with a Reconfigurable Moving-Platform for Pick-and-Place Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Operating traditional serial robots in large environments are challenging due to the difficulty and exponential cost of scaling the system's workspace. Cable-Driven Parallel Robots (CDPRs), thanks to the low cost of cables in comparison to more sophisticated mechanisms, have the possibility to operate across large workspaces with limited cost. However, one issue for CDPR remains the more complex handling of cable collisions with the environment, in particular when operating in cluttered environments that are typical in large warehouses. The following work presents a solution to this problem through the use of a reconfigurable Mobile Platform. The mechanical design and control strategy are proposed and discussed. A reconfigurable dual-platform design and unique cable routing inside the CDPR's mobile platform make it possible to increase the robot reachability. Using only the main robot motors and a docking system between the mobile platform and the work-cell ceiling, the system can dock throughout the entire workspace and deploy a sub-robot capable of operating between obstacles increasing the reachability of the robot. Two different docking system design are tested using dedicated control strategy and compared. The prototypes are experimentally validated and compared using a large scale eight cables CDPR.

articleTitle: On the Singularity Analysis of Origami Using Graph and Screw Theories
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the mobility and redundancies of an origami in its fully unfolded, partially folded, and fully folded configurations by applying graph and screw theories via Davies' method. It seeks to take advantage of the existing analogies between origami and spherical mechanisms to apply the Davies method in the kinematic analysis of origami. A detailed calculation of the mobility of two origamis is performed, identifying redundant constraints in each configuration. In addition, the singular positions of the origami in each state are explored, providing an in-depth understanding of their behavior under different conditions. These results not only provide a comprehensive insight into origami kinematics, but also have significant implications for the design and application of origami-inspired mechanisms in various fields, ranging from robotics to structural engineering.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modelling of a Four-Fingered Metamorphic Anthropomorphic Hand on Precision Grasp
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: For a metamorphic robotic hand with a foldable palm, its finger operation planes change with palm configurations. Although this reconfigurable design can enhance the grasp flexibility, manipulation workspace and application adaptability, the hand's grasp stability cannot be guaranteed when the palm reconfigures. Especially for the four-fingered metamorphic hand performing precision grasps in anthropomorphic postures, improper control of the palm configurations can result in unsuccessful grasps, which may even lead to hand damage. This paper first displays the workspace of the four-fingered anthropomorphic hand for generating precision grasp gestures. Based on it, force-closure/-balance analyses are performed, deriving the effective precision grasp workspace for typical anthropomorphic postures classified by built mathematical definition. Grasp levels are further discussed by introducing an evaluation method which considers the minimum friction coefficient (MFC) as the quality metric. The proposed scheme gives a way to depict the grasp performance of every robotic hand configuration, without considering specific objects that are to be grasped. Dynamic changes in postures' grasp performance with palm configurations are exhibited in the end.

articleTitle: Modelling Programmable Deformation of Particle-Based Structure with Smart Hydrogels
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Grippers are widely used in many industrial applications, but are limited due to their rigid constructions and no adaptability to varying stiffness. The solution for this would be the use of soft grippers. One way to design soft grippers is to use smart materials, such as hydrogels. Hydrogel soft grippers, unlike their rigid counterparts, take advantage of smart materials' inherent responsiveness and adaptability, removing the need for external power components. To explore the possibilities of using smart hydrogel as the actuator in the soft gripper, we proposed a bilayer structure including temperature sensitive hydrogel and silicone. In order to get insight into the design of these configurations for a gripper, a model consisting of hydrogel was proposed to execute simulations using Finite Element Method (FEM) in Abaqus. The results show, that by modelling different configurations with temperature as input, information can be obtained about mechanical properties such as expansion and bending. Moreover, various forms of deformation can be attained through the utilization of programmable configurations. These configurations can be tailored to achieve deformations in diverse scenarios, including bulk material conveying or underwater applications.

articleTitle: Bat Feet-Inspired Gripper: Design and Kinematic Analysis of a Metamorphic Docking Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable docking mechanism inspired by the tendon-locking mechanism of bat claws. Designed for the rapid assembly and disassembly of robots, the mechanism aims to overcome challenging terrains for ground robots, enhancing their mobility. Utilizing parallel elastic structures, the mechanism replicates the biomechanics involved in the opening and closing of a claw. Locking and unlocking are achieved through a variable-topology ratchet and groove system. We delve into the biomimetic principles of bat hanging-locking and present a comprehensive discussion on the intricate design of the docking mechanism, supported by simulation and experimental results. Successful experiments validate that the docking mechanism fulfills design requirements, effectively rectifying docking errors and offering an efficient solution for mobile robots' rapid assembly and disassembly.

articleTitle: A Target Pose Optimization Strategy for Shipborne Stabilizing Platforms in Complex Maritime Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: In shipborne stabilizing platform research, the significant cumulative error in position estimation resulting from accelerometer data integration presents a major challenge in achieving accurate real-time ship deck positions, impacting platform pose stability. This paper proposes a target pose optimization strategy for shipborne stabilizing platforms based on the Stewart configuration. Leveraging kinematic modeling of the double-actuated platform Stewart configuration, a real-time stability index is introduced based on the upper platform pose. Additionally, a penalty term based on active joint reference positions is integrated to address safety concerns associated with acceleration integration errors or fluctuating sea conditions, mitigating potential hazardous operational conditions. The proposed target pose optimization method effectively improves upper platform real-time stability and ensures safe operation of telescopic chains in various simulation scenarios, meeting the real-time stability and operational safety requirements in challenging maritime environments.

articleTitle: Vibrating Particle Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: To overcome the limitations of traditional mono-lithic robots, roboticists have proposed modular robots, swarm robots, and soft robots that can adapt to their environment and be robust to single points of failure. However, due to their many degrees of freedom, they are complex and pose operational challenges. We introduce a novel particle robot comprising vibrating units encased by a rigid chain-link boundary that can act like a soft robot. Each unit, or particle, moves by adjusting the spin direction and frequency of an internal off-axis spinning mass. The particles are simple and incapable of directed locomotion, but once combined in a particle robot, they produce deterministic motion from stochastic particle interactions. This study delves into the vibrating particle mechanism, revealing how collective movement emerges from simple, individual actions. Experimental analyses across various configurations highlight how particle quantity influences movement and direction. Notably, the robot's ability to traverse tight spaces and flow around obstacles underscores its adaptability, achieved through rigid components mimicking soft-robotics principles. Our findings illuminate the potential of harnessing stochastic interactions for deterministic outcomes, advancing the field towards more adaptable and resilient robotic systems.

articleTitle: Miniature Reconfigurable Modular Soft Robots Using Liquid Crystal Elastomer Actuation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: Soft robotics is rapidly evolving, fueled by advancements in controllable materials. Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) stand out with their exceptional actuation capabilities, ease of processing, and built-in programmability. However, current LCE robots struggle with limited dexterity and adaptability, hindering their real-world potential. We address this limitation by introducing a novel modular design approach that unlocks the full potential of LCEs. Our miniature, highly deformable soft robot utilizes reconfigurable LCE modules for bending and twisting, enabling enhanced manipulability through serial combinations. Demonstrating its dexterity, the modular robot performs intricate fingertip manipulation, allowing a miniature gripper to rotate a small object. This achievement highlights the reconfigurability and utility of our system, paving the way for more dexterous and versatile LCE-based robots.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Reconfigurable Integrated Leg-Arm Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The 4-limbed integrated leg-arm robot, which combines the manipulation capabilities of dual-arm manipulators and the stable mobility of 4-limbed climbing robots, has gained attention in various application fields. However, existing robots typically rely on increasing actuators or independent-driven reconfigurable mechanisms to meet diverse workspace requirements, resulting in increased payload and energy consumption. To tackle this challenge, this paper proposes a novel reconfigurable robot with an underactuated chassis mechanism. The chassis mechanism is established through configuration synthesis and analysis, while its underactuated behavior is revealed through degree of freedom (DOF) analysis and kinematic modeling. Finally, the feasibility of underactuation is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Model-Based Prediction Approach for Frequency Response Function of a Magnetic Adsorption Machining Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Reconfigurable Mechanisms and Robots (ReMAR)
abstract: The adsorption machining robot is an important branch of robotic machining equipment. Influenced by the low-stiffness structure, the robot's machining efficiency is significantly limited by vibration deformations. The frequency response function (FRF) is an essential theoretical foundation for analyzing cutting stability to control vibration deformations. However, characterized by adsorption interfaces and parallel structures, modeling adsorption machining robots to predict the FRF is challenging. This paper proposes a model-based prediction approach combined with parameter identification to predict the FRF of adsorption machining robots.
